newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel up, low sulphur down, again.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel up, low sulphur down, again.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil cargoes were steady to weaker on Friday while low sulphur strengthened again, traders said.
High sulphur barges were firmer at around $87/$88 and dealers said they expected a little firmness next week with the closure for maintenance of a small Rotterdam refinery.
High sulphur cargoes were heard offered at $85 cif NWE after trading at that level on Thursday. But business was quiet.

Low sulphur cargoes were firmer. An NWE refiner was heard to have sold a cargo out of southern Spain at a robust $102 fob, some $6 a tonne above March swaps levels. This deal follows business late on Thursday at $100.

Dealers said that while the prices appeared a overdone, supply was tight in northwest Europe after various purchases in the last few days which have soaked up some of the available volume. Refinery closures for maintenance in the U.K., Scandinavia and France will add to the current tightness.
And arbitrage business from the U.S. was not thought workable, even with firmer NWE prices, because of the difficulty of finding appropriate ships.
